entries: The Sith Reaver's force and melee attacks are enhanced by its fury adding +3 to any damage rolls the Reaver makes (included).

trait.name: Force Enhanced attacks
entries: The Sith Reaver's primary {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil} attacks are enhanced by it's precision and the force adding an extra 2d8 to melee strikes (included).

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Sith Reaver is a 9th level forcecaster it's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (force save DC 15, +7 to hit with force attacks, 18 force points). The Sith Reaver knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

action.name: Multiattack
entries: When the Sith Reaver makes two {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil} attacks and can chose to make 1 additional light foil attack or two offhand {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil} attacks.

action.name: Lightfoil
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 20 ({@dice 3d8+5} + 3)

action.name: Off hand Lightfoil
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 11 ({@dice 1d8+5} + 3)

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The dark lord has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The dark lord is an 18th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Wisdom (power save DC 17, +9 to hit with force attacks) and it has 77 force points. The dark lord knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

action.name: Lightfoil
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 ({@dice 1d8+2}) energy damage.

trait.name: Charger
entries: The juggernaut can take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, and if the juggernaut moves at least 10 feet in a straight line with this {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, it gains a 5 bonus to it's next melee attack’s damage roll.

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The juggernaut has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Scornful Rebuke
entries: When a creature hits the juggernaut with an attack, it takes 4 psychic damage as long as the juggernaut is not {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}.

trait.name: Shield Master
entries: If the juggernaut is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to only take half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Titan's Power
entries: The juggernaut can wield a two handed weapon in one hand. Also if he misses with an attack the creature takes 5 energy damage.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The juggernaut is an 19th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 18, +10 to hit with force attacks) and it has 42 force points. The juggernaut knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The juggernaut makes three {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} pike attacks or casts a power and makes a {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} pike attack.

action.name: Lightsaber pike
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 11} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 19 ({@dice 1d10}+{@dice 2d8+5}) energy damage.

action.name: Conquering Presence (1/Day)
entries: Each creature within 30 feet of the juggernaut must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC 18) or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of the juggernaut for 1 minute, and have its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} reduced to 0. At the end of each of its turns, a {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} creature takes 4 psychic damage and repeats this save, ending the effect on a success.

monster.name: Dark Disciple
resist: kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced weapons, damage from force powers

trait.name: Avoidance
entries: If the Dark Disciple is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to only take half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if it fails.

trait.name: Battle Precognition
entries: Dark Disciple casts {@spell Battle Precognition|sw5e-phb|battle precognition} on herself every morning.

trait.name: Cunning Action
entries: On each of its turns, the Dark Disciple can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to take the Dash, Disengage, or {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} action.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: When the Dark Disciple fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Surprise Attack (1/rest)
entries: If the Dark Disciple surprises a creature and hits it with an attack on the Dark Disciple's first turn in combat, the attack deals an extra 2d6 damage to it.

trait.name: Two-Weapon Defense
entries: The Dark Disciple gains a +1 bonus to AC while wielding a weapon in each hand (included).

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Dark Disciple is a 14th level forcecaster it's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (force save DC 19, +11 to hit with force attacks, 42 force points). The Dark Disciple knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Dark Disciple makes two {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil} attacks and can chose to make 1 additional light foil attack or two offhand {@item Lightfoil|sw5e-phb|lightfoil} attacks.

action.name: Lightfoil
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 10} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 23 ({@dice 4d8+7})

action.name: Off hand Lightfoil
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 10 ({@dice 1d8+7})

reaction.name: Parry
entries: Dark Disciple adds 6 to her AC against one melee attack that would hit her. To do so, Dark Disciple must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Dark Disciple can move up to her {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

legendary.name: Forcecasting
entries: Dark Disciple casts an at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

legendary.name: Saber
entries: Dark Disciple makes one Saber attack.

legendaryHeader: The Dark Disciple can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Dark Disciple regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: Sith Dreadlord
immune: ion and energy damage from unenhanced weapons

trait.name: Light Weapon Expert
entries: Once per turn when the dreadlord rolls damage for a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} using a {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} it can reroll the weapon’s damage dice and use either total.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: When the dreadlord fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The dreadlord is a 20th level forcecaster it's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (force save DC 20, +12 to hit with force attacks, 60 force points). The dreadlord knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The dreadlord has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against a {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Yorik Coral Exoskeloton
entries: Unless the damage from a single attack or effect exceeds 15 points, the dreadlord takes no damage from that attack. If the dreadlord takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, it takes damage as normal.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dreadlord can use his Frightful Presence. He then makes two {@item Martial lightsaber|sw5e-phb|martial lightsaber} attacks and can chose to make 1 additional {@item Martial lightsaber|sw5e-phb|martial lightsaber} attack or two offhand {@item Martial lightsaber|sw5e-phb|martial lightsaber} attacks.

action.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Each creature of the dreadlord's choice that is within 90 feet of the dreadlord and aware of him must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature’s {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to Dreadlord's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Martial Lightsaber
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 15} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 24 ({@dice 4d8+8})

action.name: Off hand Martial Lightsaber
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. *Hit* 24 ({@dice 4d8+8})

reaction.name: Parry
entries: The Dreadlord adds 7 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, the dreadlord must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The dreadlord moves up to his {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

legendary.name: Forcecasting
entries: The dreadlord casts an at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

legendary.name: Saber
entries: The dreadlord makes one {@item Martial lightsaber|sw5e-phb|martial lightsaber} attack.

legendaryHeader: The Sith Dreadlord can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Sith Dreadlord regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: First Order Warlord
resist: kinetic and energy from unenhanced weapons

trait.name: Disarming Strike (3/day)
entries: When the Warlord hits on an attack he can try to disarm the target. The Warlord adds 1d8 to the damage and the target must succeed a DC 21 Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or drop the item they are holding.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Warlord is a 15th level forcecaster it's {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (force save DC 20, +12 to hit with force attacks, 45 force points). The Warlord knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Great Weapon Fighting
entries: The Warlord can reroll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a melee attack. The Warlord must use the new roll.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: When Warlord fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Reckless
entries: At the start of its turn, the Warlord can gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on all {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack rolls} during that turn, but {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against it have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Relentless (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: If the Warlord takes 30 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it is reduced to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While wearing no armor and not wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, the Warlord adds his Constitution modifier to AC.

trait.name: Unstable Kyber Crystal
entries: The Warlords greatsaber is able to bypass resistances and immunities to energy damage. The Warlord attacks score a critical on a roll of 18-20.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: When the Warlord makes three greatsaber attacks.

action.name: Greatsaber
entries: *Melee Weapon Attack*: +13 to hit, range 5 ft., one target. *Hit* 20 (2d8+2d6+6) energy damage.

reaction.name: Force Immobilize
entries: When the first Warlord is hit by a ranged attack, before damage is applied he can use his {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to attempt to stop the attack. The Warlord rolls 1d20+12. If the result is greater than or equal to the initial attack, the Warlord can stop the projectile in an open space between the target and himself. The Warlord can then use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on his turn to unfreeze or redirect the projectile.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Warlord can move up to his {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

legendary.name: Forcecasting
entries: Warlord can cast an at-will {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

legendary.name: Martial Lightsaber
entries: Warlord makes one {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb} attack.

legendaryHeader: The First Order Warlord can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The First Order Warlord regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: Sith Betrayer
immune: kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced weapons

trait.name: Deceiver
entries: The sith betrayer has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) checks.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Sith Betrayer is an 20th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 20, +12 to hit with force attacks) and it has 85 force points. The Betrayer knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The sith has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and effects.

trait.name: Hidden from the Force
entries: The sith betrayer cannot be detected using {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Pinpoint Power
entries: When it casts a power that allows it to force creatures in an area to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the sith can instead spend 1 force point and make a ranged force attack against a single target that would be in the range. On a hit the target suffers the effects as though they failed their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

trait.name: Refocused Power
entries: When the sith is forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power, it can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and spend 2 force points to automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

trait.name: Steal the Force
entries: When the sith betrayer reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it gains 6 force points, up to its maximum.

trait.name: Storm of Sabers
entries: The sith betrayer adds 6 to its AC and Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The sith betrayer makes three saber storm attacks, or it casts a power and makes a saber storm attack.

action.name: Saber Storm
entries: *Melee or Ranged Power Attack:* +12 to hit, range 40 ft., one target. *Hit:* 19 (3d8+6) energy damage.

action.name: Sever Connection (Recharge 6)
entries: The sith betrayer targets a creature within 60 feet that can cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and attempts to disrupt their ability to use the force. The target creature must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a success, nothing happens. On a failure, the target creature is unable to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and any attempt results in the power failing. Affected creatures can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of subsequent turns, ending the effect on a success.

legendary.name: At-Will Power
entries: The sith betrayer casts an at-will power.

legendary.name: Saber Storm
entries: The sith betrayer makes a saber storm attack.

legendary.name: Forcecasting (1 legendary action per power level)
entries: Sith Betrayer can cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} by spending a number of legendary actions equal to the power level.

legendary.name: Destroy the Force (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The sith betrayer uses its Sever Connection action if its available. A creature that fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} takes an added 45 (10d8) psychic damage.

legendaryHeader: The Sith Betrayer can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Sith Betrayer regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: Sith Anathema
resist: poison; kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced attacks

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Sith Anathema is an 14th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 19, +11 to hit with force attacks) and it has 61 force points. The Sith Anathema knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Pinpoint Power
entries: When it casts a power that allows it to force creatures in an area to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the anathema can instead spend 1 force point and make a ranged force attack against a single target that would be in the range. On a hit the target suffers the effects as though they failed their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

trait.name: Refocused Power
entries: When the anathema is forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power, it can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and spend 2 force points to automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The Sith Anathema regains 15 hitpoints at the start of its turn, as long as it has 1 hit point.

trait.name: Retaliation Strike
entries: Whenever it deals damage, the Sith Anathema deals an additional 6 (1d12) damage, as long as it took damage since the start of its last turn.

trait.name: Upheld by the Force (2/day)
entries: As an action, the Sith can gain {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to energy and kinetic damage for one minute, or until it is reduced to 0 hitpoints.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Sith Anathema makes two {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb} attacks and one Necrotic Strike attack.

action.name: Lightsaber
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 12} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 19 ({@dice 3d8+6}) energy damage.

action.name: Necrotic Strike
entries: *Melee Power Attack:* +11 to hit, range 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or have their hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. Creatures that have their hitpoint maximum reduced to 0 by this attack are slain instantly.

action.name: The Force Unleashed (Recharge 6)
entries: As an action, the Anathema can choose a point within 60 feet. Each creature of its choice within 30 feet of that point must make a DC 19 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 27 (5d10) force damage and suffers 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and does not suffer {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

reaction.name: Force Shield
entries: In response to an attack, the Sith Anathema can surround itself in force energy. Until the start of its next turn, the Sith Anathema adds 5 to its AC.

monster.name: Sith Devourer
immune: poison; kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced weapons
languages: Understands Sith and {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb} but rarely speaks

trait.name: Aura of Hunger
entries: The sith gains 10 (3d6) temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} whenever a creature dies within 20 feet of it.

trait.name: Devourer of Life
entries: Enemies have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws} while within 30 feet of the sith devourer.

trait.name: Eternal (1/rest)
entries: If the sith devourer takes damage that would reduce it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it is reduced to 1 hit point instead. The sith cannot use this ability again until after a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The sith devourer is an 20th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 20, +12 to hit with force attacks) and it has 85 force points. The sith knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Force Detection
entries: The Sith can sense the presence and direction of a cast {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} within 120 ft.

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The Sith has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/day)
entries: If the sith fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While the the glutton is wearing no armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, its AC includes its Consitution modifier.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The sith glutton makes three {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} attacks. It can replace one attack with a {@spell Drain Life|sw5e-phb|drain life} attack.

action.name: Lightsaber
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 ({@dice 3d8+4}) energy damage.

action.name: Drain Life
entries: *Melee Power Attack:* +12. to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 19 (4d6+5) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken from this attack, and the sith regains an equal number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

action.name: The Hungering Void (Recharge 5-6)
entries: The sith devourer draws all force energy in a 30-foot radius toward it. Every creature of the sith’s choosing in the affected area takes 18 (4d6+5) necrotic damage, or half damage with a successful DC 20 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the sith glutton gains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to half the damage taken.

reaction.name: Rebuke of Annihilation
entries: When the sith devourer takes damage from a creature it can see within 60 feet, the attacker takes necrotic damage equal to half the damage it did to the sith.

legendary.name: At-Will Power
entries: The Sith Devourer casts an at-will power.

legendary.name: Drain Life
entries: The Sith Devourer uses its {@spell Drain Life|sw5e-phb|drain life} action.

legendary.name: Death Incarnate (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The Sith Devourer disrupts the flow of the force in a radius centered on itself. Until the start of the glutton’s next turn, no creature within 30 feet of it can regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

legendary.name: Vociferation of the Void (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The Sith makes a deadly sonic attack. Each creature within 20 feet of the sith must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of the sith’s next turn.

legendaryHeader: The Sith Devourer can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Sith Devourer regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: The Sith'ari
immune: kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced weapons

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/day)
entries: If the Sith’ari fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The Sith’ari is an 18th-level forcecaster. The Sith’ari’s {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 22, +14 to hit with force attacks) and it has 87 force points. The Sith’ari knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The Sith’ari has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

trait.name: Pinpoint Power
entries: When the sith’ari cast a power that allows it to force creatures in an area to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the sith’ari can instead spend 1 force point and make a ranged force attack against a single target that would be in the range. On a hit the target suffers the effects as though they failed their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

trait.name: Quickened Power
entries: When the sith’ari casts a power that has a casting time of 1 action, it can spend 2 additional force points to change the casting time to 1 {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} for this casting.

trait.name: Orbalsik Armor
entries: The Sith’ari wears armor comprised of Orbalisk parasites. While wearing the armor, the Sith’ari is immune to damage from unenhanced sources, and has {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to damage from enhanced weapons. If the Sith’ari takes Lightning damage, this trait does not function until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Orbalisk Regeneration
entries: The sith’ari regains 25 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point. If the sith’ari takes Lightning damage this trait does not function until the start of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack

monster.name: Sith Usurper

from: 19 with battle precognition, 21 with knight speed

resist: kinetic and energy damage from unenhanced attacks

trait.name: Cunning Action
entries: The sith can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to take the Dash, Disengage, or {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} action.

trait.name: Forcecasting
entries: The sith usurper is a 16th-level forcecaster. Its {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} is Charisma (power save DC 21, +12 to hit with force attacks) and it has 70 force points. The sith usurper knows the following {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}:

trait.name: Force-enhanced strikes
entries: The sith surper's attacks are considered enhanced for the purpose of overcoming damage {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} and immunity.

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The sith usurper has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and effects.

entries: If the sith usurper fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Overpower
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, the usurper can energize its {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} until the start of its next turn. A creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against an overpowered power. Attack rolls against the sith usurper have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Quickened Power
entries: When the usurper casts a power that has a casting time of 1 action, it can spend 2 additional force points to change the casting time to 1 {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} for this casting.

trait.name: Twinned Power
entries: When the sith casts a power that targets only one creature and doesn’t have a range of self, it can spend a number of additional force points equal to the power’s level to target a second creature in range with the same power (1 force point if the power is at-will).

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Doublesaber
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 18 ({@dice 3d8+5}) energy damage.

action.name: Shadow Step (Recharge 5-6)

legendary.name: Doublesaber

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: When Sith Blade Dancer fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, he can choose to succeed instead.

The {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a target's {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} is successful or the effect ends on it, the target is immune to Sith Mastermind's gaze for the next 24 hours.

trait.name: Booming Strikes

The extra damage is 1d6 for a 1st-level tech slot, plus 1d6 for each slot level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d6. The damage is the same type as the weapon damage. monster.name: Hutt Crime Lord

trait.name: Dominating Presence (1/rest)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, Hutt Crime Lord can call out to a humanoid who can understand it that is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by it or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of it to direct their next action. The target must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC 16). On a failed save, until the end of Hutt Crime Lord's next turn, the creature takes only the actions Hutt Crime Lord chooses, and doesn’t do anything that it doesn’t allow it to do.

trait.name: Innate Tech Casting
entries: The Hutt's innate tech casting ability is intelligence (tech save DC 16). It can innately cast the following powers:

trait.name: Techcasting
entries: At will: *{@spell Assess the Situation|sw5e-phb|assess the situation}*

trait.name: Techcasting
entries: 1/day: *{@spell Kolto Cloud|sw5e-phb|kolto cloud}, tactical {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}*

trait.name: Reassemble (1/rest)
entries: Hutt Crime Lord may use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to call its allies towards it. It chooses a number of creatures that it can see within 60 feet of it equal to its Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). They can use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to immediately move directly towards Hutt Crime Lord up to their movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. This movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

trait.name: Survival Instinct
entries: Hutt Crime Lord and all allies within 10 feet of it gain a bonus to their AC equal to half its Intelligence modifier (rounded down, included in {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb}).

trait.name: Tyrant's Ferocity
entries: Hutt Crime Lord has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any attack against a creature that is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by it or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of it.

action.name: Tail

The creature is then forced to make an attack on the ally instead. If the attack misses, the ally can immediately make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} against that creature as a part of that same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.

legendary.name: Overwhelming Presence
entries: Hutt Crime Lord can make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) or Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) skill check to attempt to charm or frighten a humanoid creature who can see or hear it within 60 feet. If the Hutt's check succeeds, the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by it if it used {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of it if it used {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, until the end of its next turn.

When attacking with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, this effect applies if either roll is a 7. monster.name: World Devastator, Juvenile

trait.name: Circuitry
entries: The construct has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would deal ion or lightning damage.

trait.name: Droid Manufacturing
entries: The world devastator can produce medium size droids, which it can deploy using its Deploy Droids legendary action, or which can be fought by creatures inside of the world devastator.

trait.name: Earth-Shaking
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, the world devastator can send a shock wave through the ground in a 300-foot-radius circle centered on itself. That area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for 1 minute. Each creature on the ground that is concentrating must succeed on a DC 26 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or the creature's {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} is broken.

trait.name: Heavy Shielding
entries: The world devastator employs heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} generators, making it difficult for smaller arms to damage it. Unless the damage from a single attack or effect exceeds 30 points, the world devastator takes no damage from that attack. If the world devastator takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, it takes damage as normal.

trait.name: Interior Vulnerability
entries: The world devastator's interior is vulnerable to damage done by grenades, mines and charges, unless it is immune to that damage. It also automatically fails all Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} from such effects that occur in its interior.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the world devastator fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Molecular Engine Collapse
entries: When the world devastator is reduced to zero {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} it explodes in a swath of atomic destruction. Each creature and object within 1 mile of the world devastator take 55 (10d10) kinetic damage, 55 (10d10) energy damage, and 55 (10d10) sonic damage. Each damage type can be reduced by half with a successful DC 18 {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}: Dexterity vs. kinetic, Constitution vs. energy, and Wisdom vs. sonic. Additionally, a creature that fails two or three of the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} is affected by a tear in hyperspace and appears 5d100 miles away in a random direction.

trait.name: Towering
entries: Creatures of Huge size or smaller can stand in the world devastator's space.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The world devastator makes three point-defense attacks.

action.name: Point-Defense
entries: The world devastator chooses a point within 320 ft and lets loose a barrage of {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} fire from its point defense system. Each creature in a 15ft cube around that point must succeed on a DC 26 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 26 (3d10+10) energy damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries: The world devastator makes one of the following blast attacks.

action.name: Gravitic Beam
entries: The world devastator expels a 90-foot cube of powerful localized gravity, originating from the construct. Falling damage in the area increases to 1d10 per 10 feet fallen. When a creature starts its turn within the area or enters it for the first time in a turn, including when the world devastator creates the field, it must make a DC 26 Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failure the creature is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained}. On a success the creature’s {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is halved as long as it remains in the field. A {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} creature repeats the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of its turn. The field persists until the world devastator’s blast attack recharges, and it can’t use gravitic beam consecutively.

action.name: Molecular Engine Flare
entries: The world devastator expels plasma in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 26 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 55 (13d6+10) fire damage and 55 (13d6+10) energy damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Spew Rock
entries: The world devastator expels rocky debris in a 90-foot cube. Each creature in that area must make a DC 26 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 71 (13d10) kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more is knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

legendary.name: Deploy Droids (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The world devastator manufactures a squad of droid troops. It deploys 1 B1-Battle Droid Squad. This squad appears in any unoccupied spaces within 10 ft. of the world devastator.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The world devastator makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

legendary.name: Point-Defense
entries: The world devastator makes a single attack with its point-defense.

legendary.name: Repair (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The world devastator regains 52 (5d20) {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

legendaryHeader: The World Devastator, Juvenile can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The World Devastator, Juvenile regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

monster.name: Amphistaff
immune: poison; ion and kinetic from unenhanced weapons

trait.name: Shaped Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the amphistaff to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} with a DC of 5+the damage taken, unless the damage is from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}. On a success, the amphistaff drops to 1 hit point instead.

action.name: Bite
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 ({@dice 1d4+3}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Spit Poison
entries: *{@atk rw} * {@hit 5} to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 ({@dice 1d4+3}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage and is {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} for 1 minute. On a successful one, the target takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded}. A target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Limited Force Immunity
entries: The warrior can't be affected or detected by {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 2nd level or lower. It has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against all other {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and effects.

trait.name: Transform Amphistaff
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, the warrior can change the form of its amphistaff.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The warrior can make two melee weapon attacks.

action.name: Amphistaff (Spear Form)
entries: *{@atk mw,rw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 ({@dice 1d6+2}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Amphistaff (Staff Form)
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 ({@dice 1d6+2}) kinetic damage, or 7 ({@dice 2d4+2}) kinetic damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

action.name: Amphistaff (Whip Form)
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 ({@dice 1d4+2}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

trait.name: Limited Force Immunity
entries: The warlord can't be affected or detected by {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of 5th level or lower. It has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against all other {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and effects.

trait.name: Martial Advantage
entries: Once per turn, the warlord can deal an extra 14 (4d6) damage to a creature it hits with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} if that creature is within 5 ft. of an ally of the warlord that isn't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}.

trait.name: Transform Amphistaff
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, the warlord can change the form of its amphistaff.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The warlord can make three melee weapon attacks.

action.name: Amphistaff (Spear Form)
entries: *{@atk mw,rw} * {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft. or 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 ({@dice 1d6+3}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Amphistaff (Staff Form)
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 ({@dice 1d6+3}) kinetic damage, or 8 ({@dice 2d4+3}) kinetic damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

action.name: Amphistaff (Whip Form)
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 6} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 ({@dice 1d4+3}) kinetic damage and the target must make a {@dc 13} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Leadership (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: For 1 minute, the warlord can utter a special command or warning whenever a nonhostile creature that it can see within 30 feet of it makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The creature can add a {@dice d4} to its roll provided it can hear and understand the warlord. A creature can benefit from only one Leadership die at a time. This effect ends if the warlord is {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: The warlord adds 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the warlord must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

trait.name: Anti Laser Aerosol
entries: Ranged Weapon Attacks that would deal energy damage have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} against the Fire Breather.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fire breather makes two tentacle attacks and one {@spell Flame Sweep|sw5e-phb|flame sweep} attack per round.

action.name: Tentacle
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 ({@dice 3d8+5}) kinetic damage & 6 ({@dice 2d6}) fire damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} (escape {@dc 17}) and takes 9 ({@dice 1d8+5}) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The Fire Breather can have up to four targets {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} at a time.

action.name: Flame Sweep
entries: Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 5d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren’t being worn or carried

action.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
entries: The Fire Breather exhales fire in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 17 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 56 (l6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

monster.name: Yorik-Kul Slave Soldier
languages: Understands Yuuzhan Vong but cannot speak

trait.name: Unfeeling Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the slave soldier to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} with a DC of 5+the damage taken, unless the damage is from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}. On a success, the slave soldier drops to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Psychic Link
entries: The slave soldier is linked to a Yammosk or a Dhuryam that gives it orders during combat.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The slave soldier makes two weapon attacks.

action.name: Coufee
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit* 7 ({@dice 1d8+3}) kinetic damage.

monster.name: Yammosk

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the Yammosk fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Creature Sense
entries: The Yammosk is aware of the presence of creatures within 5 miles of it that have an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. It knows the distance and direction to each creature, as well as each one's Intelligence score, but can't sense anything else about it. A creature protected by the {@spell Mind Blank|sw5e-phb|mind blank} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} can't be perceived in this manner.

trait.name: Telepathic Hub
entries: The Yammosk can use its telepathy to initiate and maintain telepathic conversations with up to ten creatures at a time. The Yammosk can let those creatures telepathically hear each other while connected in this way.

trait.name: War Coordinator
entries: The Yammosk gives all Yuuzhan Vong and their creatures {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on attack and save rolls when it is within 60ft of the Yammosk

trait.name: Force Resistance
entries: The Yammosk has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and other force effects.

trait.name: Yuuzhan Vong Biotech
entries: the Yammosk can cast certain certain powers utilizing its own biology and Yuuzhan Vong Biotech (Yuuzhan Vong biotech abilities will have the same guidelines as the force/{@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} they are named after ). The Yammosk's innate casting ability is Intelligence (power save DC 18). It can innately cast the following powers:

trait.name: Techcasting
entries: At will: *{@spell Sense Emotion|sw5e-phb|sense emotion}, {@spell Telekinesis|sw5e-phb|telekinesis}, {@spell Battle Precognition|sw5e-phb|battle precognition}*

trait.name: Techcasting
entries: 1/day each: *{@spell Dominate Mind|sw5e-phb|dominate mind}, {@spell Mind Trap|sw5e-phb|mind trap}*

action.name: Tentacle
entries: *{@atk mw} * {@hit 7} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. *Hit:* 20 ({@dice 4d8+2}) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it is {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} (escape {@dc 15}) and takes 9 ({@dice 1d8+5}) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The Yammosk can have up to four targets {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} at a time.

action.name: Mind Blast (Recharge 5-6)
entries: The Yammosk magically emits psychic energy. Creatures of the Yammosk's choice within 60 feet of it must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take 32 (5dl0+5) psychic damage and be {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} for l minute. A target can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Psychic Link
entries: The Yammosk targets one {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} creature it can {@optfeature Perceive|sw5e-phb|perceive} with its Creature Sense trait and establishes a psychic link with that creature. Until the psychic link ends, the Yammosk can {@optfeature Perceive|sw5e-phb|perceive} everything the target senses. The target becomes aware that something is linked to its mind once it is no longer {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, and the Yammosk can terminate the link at any time (no action required). The target can. use an action on its turn to attempt to break the psychic link, doing so with a successful DC 18 Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a successful save, the target takes 10 (3d6} psychic damage. The psychic link also ends if the target and the Yammosk are more than 5 miles apart, with no consequences to the target. The Yammosk can form psychic links with up to ten creatures at a time.

action.name: Battle Coordination
entries: The Yammosk can use its action to allow up to 10 Yuuzhan Vong creatures to use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to either to make an attack or move up to their movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

action.name: Sense Thoughts
entries: The Yammosk targets a creature with which it has a psychic link. The Yammosk gains insight into the target's reasoning, its emotional state, and thoughts that loom large in its mind (including things the target worries about, loves, or hates). The Yammosk can also make a Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}} check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} to {@optfeature Deceive|sw5e-phb|deceive} the target's mind into thinking it believes one idea or feels a particular emotion. The target contests this attempt with a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}} check. If the Yammosk succeeds, the mind believes the deception for l hour or until evidence of the lie is presented to the target.

legendary.name: Break Concentration
entries: The Yammosk targets a creature within 120 feet of it with which it has a psychic link. The Yammosk breaks the creature's {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power it has cast. The creature also takes ld4 psychic damage per level of the power.

legendary.name: Psychic Pulse
entries: The Yammosk targets a creature within 120 feet of it with which it has a psychic link. Enemies of the Yammosk within 10 feet of that creature take 10 (3d6} psychic damage.

legendary.name: Tentacle attack
entries: The Yammosk makes a tentacle attack.

trait.name: Spiked Hide

monsterFluff.name: 1.4 FD P-Tower Turret
entries: The t'landa Til are a massive, quadrupedal, sentient species distantly related to the Hutts. They possess long, thin, whipping tails and four trunk-like legs with huge, padded feet. They also have a tiny pair of arms with delicate hands, each with four fingers. Their faces resemble those of the Hutts save for a long, thick horn above their snout. Like the Hutts, their necks are short and humped—almost nonexistent. They have thick, oily, leathery skin, which hangs in creases, wrinkles, and loose folds. This skin is especially prominent below the neck, where it hangs so loose that it hides the arms when they are folded against the chest.

The t'landa Til also have two hearts and three stomachs. Male t'landa Til make a sound that attracts females during mating season. This humming vibration is produced when air flows over the cilia in a male's inflated neck pouch. This vibration stimulates a female's pleasure centers. This ability is accompanied by the males' low-grade {@feat Empathic|sw5e-phb|empathic} ability, which they use to {@spell Project|sw5e-phb|project} pleasant feelings toward females. The t'landa Til can use this same pouch to create sonic and subsonic vibrations with powerful effects on other species. The average t'landa Til stands about 2 - 2.5 meters tall.

entries.name: 1.4 FD P-Tower
entries: Manufactured by Atgar SpaceDefense Corporation, the 1.4 FD P-Tower is a light laser cannon employed as a fixed emplacement anti-vehicle weapon. It is designed to target a variety of enemy vehicles, including repulsortanks and landspeeders, although it has difficulty targeting fast-moving vehicles. The unit is quick to produce and inexpensive.

The main bulk of the weapon is a 2.8 meter high energy dish that has sixteen micropower routers spaced evenly along the outer edge, and eight power conversion cells along the interior of the dish. Targeting sensors are placed on the upper edge of the dish, and a single light laser cannon emanates from the center of the dish. To fire the weapon, energy is fed directly into each micropower router which holds the {@optfeature Charge|sw5e-phb|charge} until the firing computer registers that the Energy Conversion Point had been achieved. The power conversion cells around the dish glows once the weapon is primed to fire. At that point, the firing computer channels the energy from the routers into the main power converter located at the center of the dish, firing the weapon. The energy beam moves through the discharge barrel, into the galven circuitry and through the focusing lens to produce a low-power beam that is effective against repulsorcraft, landspeeders, and airspeeders.

The 1.4 FD P-Tower utilizes an Atgar C-6 battery, which only retains enough power for eight shots before needing to be replaced. The battery is easy to replace when handled by a skilled technician. When hooked up to a power generator, the weapon has unlimited fire capability. The weapon also suffers from a low fire rate, and requires ten seconds to build up an adequate {@optfeature Charge|sw5e-phb|charge}.
The visible dish was also a tempting target for opponents, although the weapon itself is protected by {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor} plating.

entries.name: AT-DP
entries: The All Terrain Defense Pod (AT-DP) was a bipedal Imperial walker manufactured by Kuat Drive Yards prior to and during the Galactic Civil War. They were driven by Imperial combat drivers.

The AT-DP walker, a successor to the AT-RT, serves as the mainstay of backwater garrisons and support for larger war machines, including the AT-AT. Unlike the AT-ST, a shorter bipedal walker boasting a host of armaments, the AT-DP is armed only with a single Maad-38 heavy laser cannon. The weapon is powerful enough to destroy another walker of the same type. The cockpit has seating for a driver and a gunner, with the gunner situated behind the driver, although both crewmen can move the walker, fire the cannon, and have access to the gyroscopic controls used to keep the walker stable. Each of these walkers has a hatch at the top to access the cockpit; a main viewport at the front, with bulbs on the side and slits to improve visibility; and holographic projectors.

Each walker possesses armor strong enough to protect from {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} fire. Missile launchers and explosives are effective against the walkers, however. Although the walkers are sturdy, their heads are {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone} to exploding under sustained duress.

AT-DPs were used throughout the Empire to keep the populations of occupied worlds in line and to combat insurgent forces. Many of these walkers were used in Imperial Academies for both defensive purposes and training cadets. Two walkers can be attached to the underside of a Gozanti-class cruiser for landing in almost any suitable environment.

monsterFluff.name: Alpha-class ARC Trooper
entries: Clone commandos were elite clone troopers that served in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. A result of the Kaminoans' genetic experimentation with Jango Fetts genes and elite training, they were equipped with grenades, sabotage gear, and the DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System. They choose the colors on their armor.

monsterFluff.name: Ambush Master
entries: A bounty hunter is an individual hired to capture, hunt or eliminate a designated target, depending on their clients' wishes.

Some bounty hunters act like mercenaries and are hired to do jobs other than tracking down bounties. Hutts often keep these mercenary hunters on retainer so as to have more experienced and capable bodyguards protecting them.

When the bounty hunting guild assigns one of its members to pursue the subject of a government bounty, only that particular hunter is authorized to go after that particular acquisition. Members of the Guild are required to follow the Bounty Hunter Code. The Code notably forbids the slaying of another hunter, or stealing another hunter's bounty. It also forbids hunters from asking about their bounties once delivered, requiring that the events that transpired from accepting the bounty to its delivery to be immediately forgotten.

During the reign of the Galactic Empire, the guild was given authority by the Imperial Office of Criminal {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb} to issue Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificates, which allowed its holder access to the Imperial Enforcement DataCore.

monsterFluff.name: Amphistaff
entries: The Yuuzhan Vong—"Children of Yun-Yuuzhan", also called the Chosen Race, known to the Chiss and Ferroans as the Far Outsiders, and sometimes incorrectly abbreviated to Vong (which implied that one was disowned by their family and their gods)—were a sentient species that nearly destroyed the New Republic, and were responsible for the deaths of nearly 365 trillion sentient beings during their invasion of the galaxy.

{@b {@i Biology & Appearance.}} The Yuuzhan Vong are humanoids that are taller and of heavier build than the average Human. Yuuzhan Vong also have a life span generally around three times that of a Human's. Yuuzhan Vong have sloping, almost ridge-like foreheads. Some have pointed ears, while some do not. This disparity could be due to ritual mutilations, or a genetic variation; there is no conclusive evidence as to what the species' norm is. Yuuzhan Vong also have short, stub-like noses, making their faces appear skull-like. They usually have black hair, though in lesser amounts on both the head and body than Humans, but often wear it much longer than them, unless completely bald. Small blue sacks can be found under the eyes of the Yuuzhan Vong, and they are often considered a mark of beauty. These eyesacks expand and contract to reflect a Yuuzhan Vong's mood. The most common skin tones among the Yuuzhan Vong are gray and yellow, and their blood is jet black. The Yuuzhan Vong nervous system is very conductive, as if it was made specifically for feeling pain.

{@b {@i The Force.}} Perhaps the most notable and most objectionable trait of the Yuuzhan Vong is that they are outside of the Force: they have no Force presence that can be sensed, and are unaffected by most {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that are targeted directly at them. Any attempt to sense their motivation or truthfulness or to determine their next course of action is futile. Although it is not possible to affect the Yuuzhan Vong directly through the use of the Force, it is possible to use indirect means to accomplish such a task, such as manipulating an object through {@spell Telekinesis|sw5e-phb|telekinesis} and throwing it at a Yuuzhan Vong, which would injure them, or by controlling the air in an attempt to increase the pressure, thus allowing a Jedi to, in effect, crush the Yuuzhan Vong.

{@b {@i Culture.}} Yuuzhan Vong culture is centered on sacrifice, their gods, and the philosophy of pain. They glorify pain; not as a motive for action, but as a state of living. They believe that, just like their gods had sacrificed their bodies to create the galaxy, the Yuuzhan Vong themselves were to sacrifice parts of their body for a greater purpose. By remaking their own bodies, they are becoming closer to their deities. However, they never maim their bodies in a manner that would permanently hinder their ability to function. Individual Yuuzhan Vong have mottling or scarring, and sweeping tattoos. The more elite individuals are even known to graft organs from other creatures into their bodies. Devotional practices to the gods call for bloodletting at prayer times.

The Yuuzhan Vong employ a caste system including warriors, shapers, priests, intendants and workers. Love affairs between two different castes is considered forbidden. They also greatly believe in honor: even under interrogations, the word of a Yuuzhan Vong is high, and, if they promise respite to their victims for revealing information, they typically keep their word. There also exists a similar concept to the Wookiee Life debt, which is known as Us-hrok.

{@b {@i Technology.}} The Yuuzhan Vong have a fanatical hatred of machines, believing them to be abominations and an affront to their gods. Machines do not die, meaning that they are capable of replacing organic life—which is something the Yuuzhan Vong would never allow.

entries.name: Warrior Caste
entries: The warrior caste served as the armies of the Yuuzhan Vong and was one of the largest castes who essentially served as the military branch of their race. Members of the caste were trained from an early age to excel in combat. Warriors were also more aggressive than other Yuuzhan Vong. Their chief weapon was the amphistaff, which resembled a deadly serpent capable of spitting venom or coiling around foes. The warriors were devotees of the Slayer, Yun-Yammka, and sought honor in combat. They wore the living vonduun crab armor which was capable of resisting {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} fire or lightsabers. This armor did have weak points, such as points at the armpit and areas of the inner hip where the shell's segments joined.
Ranks of the warrior caste included the Warmaster, Supreme Commander, Commander, Subaltern and Warrior.

monsterFluff.name: Anzellan Droidsmith
entries: Away from polished society lies a darker realm shrouded in secrets and forgotten under layers of grime. The underworld of the galaxy includes all manner of denizens and visitors to its seedy realm. Thugs, gamblers, smugglers, bounty hunters, professional companions, criminals, and crooks all scrape by, making a living through illegal and morally adjacent pursuits.

monsterFluff.name: Aqualish Enforcer
entries: Away from polished society lies a darker realm shrouded in secrets and forgotten under layers of grime. The underworld of the galaxy includes all manner of denizens and visitors to its seedy realm. Thugs, gamblers, smugglers, bounty hunters, professional companions, criminals, and crooks all scrape by, making a living through illegal and morally adjacent pursuits.

entries.name: Thugs & Security Forces
entries: Various different types of thugs and security forces, appropriate for gangs, simple ruffians, or mercenaries.

monsterFluff.name: Aquatic Jedi Master
entries: The Jedi Order is an ancient order of protectors united by their ability to harness the power of the Force. Adhering to a doctrine that favored the light side of the Force, the Jedi aspire to attain a state of inner tranquility through calmness and meditation while avoiding emotions affiliated with the dark side of the Force, such as anger and hatred. Nevertheless, Jedi philosophy does not forbid a Jedi from acting in self-defense or in the defense of others. To that end, the weapon of a Jedi is the {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber}, a blade composed of pure energy and different colors such as blue, green, purple or yellow.

{@b {@i History.}} Before the time of the Galactic Empire, a Jedi was a guardian of peace and justice in the Galactic Republic. The Jedi's commitment to peace and democracy brought them into conflict with an order of dark side wielders known as the Sith, who sought power and dominion over the galaxy. Emerging victorious from their wars with the ancient Sith, the Jedi carried on in their duty as peacekeepers for over a millennium until the advent of the Clone Wars twenty-two years before the Battle of Yavin. Faced with a pan-galactic civil war between the Republic and Confederacy of Independent Systems, the Jedi adopted the mantle of generals and soldiers in the Grand Army of the Republic. After three years of conflict, the Jedi discovered that the war had been a ploy designed to restore the Sith to power. However, the Jedi were betrayed by one of their own—the Chosen One, Anakin Skywalker, who had been seduced to the dark side and anointed Darth Vader by the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. Using the Jedi's own clone troopers to initiate a systematic purge of the Jedi Order, the Lords of the Sith all but eradicated the Jedi in one fell swoop, reducing the order from thousands of Jedi Knights to a handful of survivors who dispersed into exile across the galaxy.

After Luke Skywalker redeemed his father, Anakin, and destroyed the Sith, the New Republic was founded. During the era of the New Republic, Skywalker worked to rebuild the Jedi Order by training many apprentices.

{@b {@i Philosophy.}} The Jedi Knights focus on calmness and peace to channel their powers in the Force, using the light side of the Force to serve in the capacity of guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy. Even so, the Jedi seek to preserve balance in the Force; the ancient prophecy of the Chosen One foretold of a being who would restore balance to the Force by destroying the Sith. In combat, whereas an enemy may grow impatient and rely on their overwhelming strength, a Jedi would meditate and find serenity in their mind to focus. A Jedi uses their {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} only for defense, not for attack, and uses the Force for defense and knowledge rather than using it to gain power over others. Because of this, some Jedi are capable of appearing after death as Force spirits. Knowledge, the Force, and self-discipline are considered the three pillars of Jedi strength.

Some members of the Jedi Order had specific titles and roles within the Order. These included:

entries.name: Jedi Knight
entries: Jedi Knight was a rank within the Jedi Order, referring to Jedi who had completed their training and passed the Jedi Trials to become a full member of the Order. Jedi Knights, like the Order they served, were guardians of peace and justice in the Galactic Republic, and served in key military command roles during the Clone Wars. At the war's end, Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine—secretly the Sith Lord Darth Sidious—issued Order 66, declaring every Jedi an enemy of the state. As a result, the clone troopers of the Grand Army of the Republic turned against their generals, killing most of the Jedi Knights. At the end of the Galactic Civil War, Luke Skywalker was the last known Jedi Knight.

monsterFluff.name: ARC Trooper
entries: Clone commandos were elite clone troopers that served in the Grand Army of the Republic during the Clone Wars. A result of the Kaminoans' genetic experimentation with Jango Fetts genes and elite training, they were equipped with grenades, sabotage gear, and the DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System. They choose the colors on their armor.

entries.name: Designated ARC Troopers
entries: During the war, the shortening supply of ARCs and their high demand for tactical missions forced the GAR to look for clone troopers to fill their role. As early as 21 BBY, clone troopers who demonstrated exceptional ability could be promoted to ARC trooper and would receive similar duties, though they were not genetically engineered in the same ways as the Alpha and Null classes and lacked ARC training. In this manner, clone troopers Fives and Echo of the 501st Legion were given the designation of ARC Trooper following their successful defense of Kamino.

entries.name: Assassins
entries: Members of the profession are referred to by many euphemisms and epithets: "problem solvers" in the Corporate Sector Authority, "exterminators" in the Outer Rim Territories, and "slayers" in the Core Worlds. Whatever their name, most professional assassins are concerned solely with credits, though some kill for political or religious reasons, or merely for love of killing. This makes assassins simultaneously the best-paid and most-despised members of the galaxy's underworld.
Though assassination is illegal on most planets, on some, such as Umbara, assassinations are a relatively normal part of society.

entries.name: AT-PT
entries: The All Terrain Personal Transport (AT-PT) is a light anti-infantry walker used by the Galactic Republic and, later, the Galactic Empire. It is manufactured by Rothana Heavy Engineering, a subsidiary of Kuat Drive Yards. They were precursors to the AT-ST and AT-AT.
AT-PTs are made to take single troopers into intense combat situations on their own, with the firepower of a squad. They stand only three meters tall, and are driven by AT-PT pilots.

The walkers are capable of reaching speeds up to 60 kilometers per hour and can climb a 45-degree angle, with hydraulic adjusters keeping the unit balanced. The vehicles carry a long-range comm antenna for patrols. The main drive unit provides power and hydraulic pressure for the two legs, and features cooling vents. The cockpit entry hatch is on the side, while the emergency flare launcher is just above the viewport.

The AT-PT is — compared to its intended threat, enemy soldiers — heavily armored, enough so that small-arms fire cannot penetrate the craft's armor. The walker is armed with twin {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} cannons and one concussion grenade launcher, which are only effective against infantry. The walker's superior agility made up for its {@filter light armor|items|type=light armor} (in comparison to most other cavalry units).
The units often travel in packs for increased firepower.
The AT-PT was a limited production model, the majority of which were stationed aboard the Dreadnaught-class cruisers of the legendary Katana fleet, and many were lost when the fleet itself vanished.
During the Galactic Civil War, the Galactic Empire utilized a number of the walkers. They were often used as sentries and patrol vehicles near Imperial installations.

monsterFluff.name: Ax-108 "Ground Buzzer" Sentry Gun
entries: The t'landa Til are a massive, quadrupedal, sentient species distantly related to the Hutts. They possess long, thin, whipping tails and four trunk-like legs with huge, padded feet. They also have a tiny pair of arms with delicate hands, each with four fingers. Their faces resemble those of the Hutts save for a long, thick horn above their snout. Like the Hutts, their necks are short and humped—almost nonexistent. They have thick, oily, leathery skin, which hangs in creases, wrinkles, and loose folds. This skin is especially prominent below the neck, where it hangs so loose that it hides the arms when they are folded against the chest.

The t'landa Til also have two hearts and three stomachs. Male t'landa Til make a sound that attracts females during mating season. This humming vibration is produced when air flows over the cilia in a male's inflated neck pouch. This vibration stimulates a female's pleasure centers. This ability is accompanied by the males' low-grade {@feat Empathic|sw5e-phb|empathic} ability, which they use to {@spell Project|sw5e-phb|project} pleasant feelings toward females. The t'landa Til can use this same pouch to create sonic and subsonic vibrations with powerful effects on other species. The average t'landa Til stands about 2 - 2.5 meters tall.

entries.name: Sentry Gun
entries: Sentry guns come in a wide variety of different sizes, yields, and types. These weapons can typically be found near high-value areas such as detention cells, command centers, and laboratories. For best results, they are placed in areas such as corners, above security doors, or other positions that afford them a wide field of fire. Sentry guns are usually linked to the central security system, but can be operated manually by remote. Once activated, these turrets may use active sensors and preprogrammed criteria to identify threats and fire upon any hostiles they encounter. Sentry guns are also used on starships and may automatically engage nearby hostiles and are linked to the ship's central security system. Some sentry guns include targeting sensors that seek out energy signatures from enemy weapons, with built-in computers to determine which targets pose the most immediate threat.

monsterFluff.name: B1 Battle Droid
entries: Battle droids, also known as combat droids or battle bots, are a type of droid designed for combat. One thing most battle droids have in common is limited intelligence. They are programmed to follow orders, and not much else, though they do have personalities. Some battle droids, however, have some form of intelligence. These droids are much more expensive to make, due to their advanced brains.

{@b {@i Clone Wars.}} Over the years, many different models of battle droid have been utilized by various factions throughout the galaxy. The Confederacy of Independent Systems, for example, used a number of different models of battle droid during the Clone Wars to make up the Separatist Droid Army. Under the command of General Grievous, varying models of battle droid fought against the Galactic Republic's clone troopers until the final days of the war, when the Confederate battle droids were deactivated by the Galactic Empire.

entries.name: B1 Series Battle Droids
entries: B1 battle droids, also referred to as standard battle droids, are the most widely-used battle droids manufactured by Baktoid Combat Automata and Baktoid Armor Workshop and were the successor to the OOM-series battle droids. The B1 battle droid sees extensive service as the mainlines soldiers due to their cheap, mass produced nature. The B1-X model serves as an officer unit.

{@b {@i History.}} Early versions of the model required the use of a Central Control Computer, but despite these weaknesses they saw extensive service as the mainlines soldier of the Trade Federation's mechanized droid army. Despite their limitations and despite battle droids being outlawed under the Empire, B1 battle droids continued to see use through Separatist holdouts and the black market during the Imperial Era.

entries.name: Smugglers
entries: A smuggler, also known by the euphemism free trader, is someone who engaged in the clandestine shipment of goods or people to prevent taxation or some other impediment. The goods shipped are often highly illegal or banned in some sectors. Weapon smugglers are referred to as gun runners.

By far the most commonly smuggled substances are varieties of spice. Although most kinds of spice are psychoactive drugs, and most forms were illegal under the Empire, the government's main concern is not to stem the flow of spice, but to collect taxes from its shipment and distribution through legitimate channels. Weapons were another commonly smuggled commodity within the Empire, whose bureaucracy strictly controlled weapons availability in order to prevent criminals and insurgents, in particular the Rebel Alliance, from becoming significant threats. Other cargo for smugglers include chak-root, stolen merchandise, and even clear water. In extreme situations, smugglers delivered standard resources or food.

entries.name: Basilisk War Droid
entries: The Basilisk war droid is a powerful, semi-sentient combat droid, designed by the Basiliskan race native to the planet Basilisk, located in the Core Worlds. Following the Mandalorian Crusaders' conquest of Basilisk in 4017 BBY, the Mandalorian warriors pillaged the powerful war droids for themselves. To the Mandalorians, the Basilisk droid was known as the Bes'uliik—the "iron beast" in the Mandalorian language of Mando'a—and came to be valued as animal-like companions.

Measuring several meters in height, Basilisk droids resemble a cross between a Zalorian rock-lion and a Karran beetle. They are armed with an array of weapons in and on their armored frame, including laser and pulse-wave cannons, shockwave generator rods, and {@spell Shatter|sw5e-phb|shatter}-missile launchers. The Mandalorians were known for riding Basilisk war droids down into the atmosphere of a world from space at tremendous speeds, using gravitational force and the {@spell Element of Surprise|sw5e-phb|element of surprise} to overwhelm their foes. Over time, the warrior culture adapted the droids to suit different combat roles, and developed new iterations of the Basilisk that included enhanced features such as a closed cockpit.

Following the Mandalorians' defeat at Malachor V in the final battle of the Mandalorian Wars, the warriors were commanded by the Jedi Knight Revan to destroy their Basilisk mounts as part of the terms of their surrender. However, not all complied with Revan's demands, and numerous Basilisk droids continued to {@optfeature Survive|sw5e-phb|survive} with Mandalorians who refused to give up their beast-like companions, including members of Clan Jendri and Clan Ordo. Even still, the war droids' numbers dwindled over time, and by the rise of the New Republic, most Baslisk droids could only be found in the museums of the galaxy.

entries.name: Black Sun
entries: Black Sun held a massive amount of reach and influence, extending its tendrils of corruption deep in the various galactic governments of each era. It was infamous for its involvement in piracy and smuggling. But smuggling was just the tip of the iceberg of the galaxy-wide organization. It was involved in every known type of illegal activity; its information networks surpassed even the accuracy and scope of Imperial Intelligence. The resources available to Black Sun rivaled those belonging to a large planetary army, including foot soldiers.
Below the leader of Black Sun were nine Vigos (Old Tionese for "nephew"). Each Vigo ruled over his or her own territory and sector.
